tokyo_teuchi_soba_towada_metro.price_note: Full menu with prices, tax included, from the shop’s own menu page. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. A hand-cut soba house near Kaminarimon with an Aomori accent — the sake list is Aomori (田酒, 七力) and the 暮坪 items use Iwate’s 暮坪かぶ, a pungent turnip grated in place of wasabi. ⚠ NOTHING HERE CLEARS EITHER DIET. Every noodle is soba or udon, the tsuyu is soy and dashi, and the tempura is wheat batter. That is stated rather than worked around. ⚠ THE ONE ITEM WORTH UNDERSTANDING IS 焼酎そば湯割り at ¥600 — shochu cut with 蕎麦湯, the cloudy water the soba was boiled in. It is the same trap recorded at 玄蕎麦しんがり: a coeliac who has avoided every bowl on the board can still be caught by a drink, because nothing in the words 焼酎 or 湯割り says noodle. ⚠ AND ONE DISH IS ONLY A PARTIAL LOSS: 豚しゃぶ at ¥2,500 per head, pre-order only and from two people, is pork and vegetables cooked in water — no batter, no noodle. Shabu-shabu sauces are ponzu and goma-dare, both soy-based, so it turns entirely on whether the kitchen will serve it with salt and citrus instead. That is the question to ask here.

⚠ THE ONLY DISH HERE WITH NO NOODLE AND NO BATTER: pork and vegetables cooked in water at the table. That makes it the one thing on a soba-house menu a coeliac could plausibly eat — and it turns on the dipping sauce, since ponzu and goma-dare are both soy-based. Ask for salt and citrus. Requires advance booking and a minimum of two people.

⚠ A DRINK MADE OF THE NOODLE WATER. 蕎麦湯 is the cloudy water the soba was boiled in — so it carries the 打ち粉 and whatever wheat was in the noodles — and nothing in the name 焼酎そば湯割り reads as a hazard to someone who has carefully avoided the food menu. The same trap appears at 玄蕎麦しんがり.
Junmai sake is rice, water and koji only — no added alcohol. The coeliac caveat is that koji is occasionally grown on barley.

tokyo_tansouan_kenjiro.price_note: tansouan.com DOES NOT RESOLVE. Google 8.8.8.8 and Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 both return SERVFAIL — the zone's nameservers are not answering, rather than the name having been withdrawn — so there was no page to read and no menu has been established. Worth one cheap DNS retry on a future tick before anyone spends a full research slot on it; a SERVFAIL is a different failure from the NXDOMAIN that 渋谷更科's domain returns. The dataset's only other link is Tabelog, which 403s from this egress. Nothing about the shop's food is recorded.

tokyo_tochigiya_shoten.price_note: THE SHOP'S ONLINE STORE HAS BEEN TAKEN DOWN. tochigiya20.thebase.in answers, but with an HTTP 302 straight to https://thebase.com/ — the platform's own marketing homepage. That is what BASE serves for a shop that has been closed or deleted, and it is a definite negative rather than an ambiguous one: the store exists as a hostname, it just has no storefront behind it any more. There is therefore no product list, no price list and no menu to read, and the dataset's website field is stale. The only other link on file is Tabelog, which serves a Cloudflare managed challenge to this egress. ⚠ WORTH NOTING FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: a thebase.in address is a mail-order storefront, not a restaurant menu, so even when it was live it would have listed retail goods at retail prices rather than a counter card — a BASE shop should never be merged into a menu record as though its product prices were dish prices. Nothing about what 栃木家商店 serves in Asakusa is established here and no item is recorded.

tokyo_kanoya_shinjuku_nishiguc.price_note: ⚠ READ THE BRANCH CAVEAT BEFORE USING THESE PRICES. かのや食品's 事業紹介 page for the 生そば・讃岐うどん かのや business publishes a 主なメニュー list of five priced lines, but the 店舗紹介 block on that same page names only ONE shop — 新宿東南口店 (新宿3-36-2 新宿キリンビル 1F, 03-3226-8633) — and this record is the 西口店. The priced list sits under the business heading rather than under that branch heading, and the page title covers 上野、新橋、新宿 collectively, so these are the brand's representative standing-soba prices rather than a card confirmed for the west-exit shop. They are recorded provisional and medium for exactly that reason; a coeliac would not be misled by them either way, because nothing on this menu is edible for one. ⚠ THE SOBA HERE IS 五割 — THE SHOP SAYS SO ITSELF. 「かのやのそばは、五割そば」: fifty per cent buckwheat, which means the other fifty per cent is wheat flour, declared by the operator on its own page. That is a much blunter fact than the usual 打ち粉 argument and it makes every soba line an outright no rather than an ask. The udon is 手打ち wheat by definition. ⚠ THE DASHI IS BOTH THE VEGAN ANSWER AND HALF THE GLUTEN ANSWER, AND THE SHOP SPELLS IT OUT. The soba dashi is 本ガツオ節・ソーダカツオ節・サバ節; the udon dashi is 瀬戸内のにぼし・利尻昆布・ウルメ・カツオ・サバ. Four of the five udon-dashi ingredients are fish, so no bowl in this shop is vegan, and a Japanese noodle tsuyu is finished with soy sauce, which is wheat-brewed unless declared tamari. ⚠ ミニカレー IS THE ONE PEOPLE ASSUME IS SAFE AND IT IS NOT: Japanese curry is thickened with a wheat-flour roux. The company also runs an unrelated 居酒屋 かのや in Ueno with its own prices; that is a different business on the same corporate site and none of it is recorded here. Drinking water at the shops is stated to be π-water, which is a marketing claim and not a dietary one.

tokyo_hashidaya_honten.price_note: はし田屋'S SITE IS LIVE AND EVERY WORD OF IT IS A PICTURE. The domain serves a Shift-JIS splash with a Flash object and three branch doors — NAKAMEGURO / SHIBUYA / SAPPORO. The Shibuya section (the one matching this record's Shibuya location) does have the right pages: /shibuya/menu/index.html is titled 「鶏料理　はし田屋　昼・夜のお品書き」, /shibuya/osusume/ is 「おすすめの料理」 and /shibuya/kodawari/ is 「素材のこだわり」. All three were fetched, decoded from Shift-JIS and read. Each returns between 2.7 and 4.3 KB of markup whose entire body is a title, a table of spacer GIFs and image tags — the お品書き itself is a scanned or typeset image, so there is no dish name and no price to extract, and there is no PDF and no text alternative. That is the finding: the menu is published, but not in any form a fetcher can read. ⚠ ONE THING IS ESTABLISHED AND IT IS THE CATEGORY: the site's own page titles call this 鶏料理 — a chicken house — and the Shibuya top page carries a 7月11日 opening-hours update, so the site is maintained rather than abandoned. ⚠ WHAT THAT IMPLIES, AND IT IS IMPLICATION NOT EVIDENCE, is that a 鶏料理 specialist in Japan is normally built on 焼鳥 with a soy-mirin タレ, 唐揚げ in a wheat-and-starch dredge, and a 親子丼 or 鶏スープ finished with soy — none of which is safe, and none of which is recorded here as an item, because the shop has published no item this machine can read. It is also unconfirmed which of the three branches is the 本店; the record's Tabelog area code points at Shibuya and that is the section that was read. Anyone revisiting this needs eyes on the images or a phone call.

tokyo_sou_san_no_gyoza_suidoba.price_note: THE SHOP'S WIX SITE PUBLISHES ITS LUNCH CARD, ITS SIDE MENU AND ITS COURSE CONTENTS AS TEXT BUT SETS EVERY PRICE AS AN IMAGE, so the dish names below are first-party and complete while the figures are almost entirely missing. The prices that ARE text are recorded: +100円 to upgrade the set rice to 魯肉飯, a 500円 wooden 木札 that makes your first drink free permanently, 100円 off a refill, and +2,000円 (税込) for two hours of nomihodai on the course. A customer review reproduced on the shop's own page reports 焼き餃子定食4個 at 850円 (税込); that is a diner's report rather than the shop's own price list and is deliberately NOT attached to the item. The shop is the Suidobashi sister of Roppongi's 餃包 and also runs a kitchen car under the name 林煎包. ⚠ THE ONE ITEM WORTH THE TRIP IS THE 豆花. Soy-milk pudding served 黒蜜きなこ — sugar syrup and roasted soybean flour — is starch-free, wheat-free and animal-free, and on a card that is otherwise wall-to-wall wheat wrappers it is the only line recorded gf AND vegan. ⚠ EVERYTHING THE SHOP IS NAMED FOR IS WHEAT. 焼き餃子, 焼売, 小籠包, 春巻き and 台湾まぜそば are all wheat dough, and 台湾まぜそば is a dry sauced noodle, which puts more soy on the plate rather than less. 油淋鶏 is fried chicken under a soy-vinegar-and-negi dressing. The ten-item 本格中華三昧コース is listed in full — 肉もやし／ザーサイ／くらげきゅうり／むし鶏のネギソース／よだれ鶏／手羽先ザンギ／シューマイ／春巻き／台湾まぜそば plus the 焼餃子 — and of those ten, ザーサイ is the only one that is plausibly plant-based, and even that is a pickle whose dressing is not described.

tokyo_gyoza_xiaolongbao_fupao_.price_note: 餃子 小籠包 福包酒場 渋谷店 (渋谷区道玄坂1丁目7-10 新大宗渋谷道玄坂一丁目ビル1F, near Shinsen) publishes its whole food and drink card on its own Gnavi shop site. Prices are 税込 and remarkably flat — most of the 一品 and 冷菜 sit at ¥429 and almost every sour is ¥429. ⚠ A DUMPLING BAR IS THE WORST POSSIBLE ROOM FOR A COELIAC and this one is a clean example of why: gyoza, shumai, spring-roll and xiaolongbao wrappers are all wheat, the 担々麺 / ジャージャー麺 / 塩鶏そば / ネギそば / 香麺 noodles are wheat, the 麻婆豆腐 is built on doubanjiang (a wheat-fermented broad-bean paste), the 唐揚げ and 油淋鶏 are wheat-coated, and the whole 一品 potato block comes out of the same fryer as all of that. ⚠ The three things a coeliac could plausibly ask about are 枝豆 (¥429), ヤミツキピリ辛キュウリ and ニンニク叩き胡瓜 (¥429 each) — but Chinese smashed-cucumber dressings are soy and black vinegar by default, so they are recorded as no rather than ask. The one dessert that stands clear is 濃厚杏仁豆腐 at ¥429: almond, sugar and dairy, no flour. ⚠ Happy hour: 16:00–18:00 drinks are discounted, conditional on one otoshi charge and one food order per person, and the shop runs a promotional 60-minute all-you-can-drink for ¥1 on weekdays 16:00–18:00 in welcome-party season.

The record's 'ask/ask' tiers look right and the card gives no reason to move them.

Composition and dressing unpublished; a Chinese-restaurant salad dressing is normally soy-and-sesame based. Ask.
The only vegetable-centred dish on the card and it is named for OYSTER SAUCE — shellfish, and Japanese-market oyster sauce routinely contains wheat.

items.ja: 直火焼きチャーシュー
items.note: Char siu marinade is soy sauce, hoisin and fermented bean curd.
Lap cheong is cured with soy sauce and rice wine as standard; house-made, so the recipe is not published. Ask.

items.ja: 豚スペアリブの豆鼓蒸し
items.en: Steamed pork spare ribs with fermented black bean
items.note: 豆鼓 fermented black bean is soy, and the steaming sauce is soy sauce with a starch coating on the ribs.

⚠ Rice porridge is the dish a coeliac will reach for and it is not automatically safe — Chinese congee is boiled in house STOCK, not water, and that stock is where the soy normally enters. Ask what the base is. Contains egg.

items.ja: 胡麻風味担々麺／本場汁なし担々麺／マーラー風味担々麺
items.romaji: goma fūmi tantanmen / honba shirunashi tantanmen / mārā fūmi tantanmen
items.en: Dan dan noodles — sesame, authentic dry-style, or mala
items.note: Wheat noodles; the sauce is sesame paste with soy, preserved mustard greens and minced pork.
Wheat noodle and wheat wonton wrapper, in a soy-seasoned broth.

Jian dui are glutinous RICE flour with red bean paste — plant-based and wheat-free in the classic recipe, which makes this the most promising item on the card for both diets. They are deep-fried, and the shop's fryer is shared. Ask.
Wheat pastry, egg custard, dairy.

items.ja: かぼちゃの焼きプリン
items.note: Egg and dairy custard; flour content not stated.

tokyo_stand_hero.price_note: ⚠ SOURCE AND DATE, BECAUSE BOTH ARE UNUSUALLY GOOD FOR A SHOP WITH NO WEBSITE: the shop’s only listed channel is a Facebook page, and Facebook returns HTTP 400 to this egress, so nothing first-party could be read. The prices below come from a standing-bar specialist site, senbero.net, whose article was first posted 2023-04-13 and re-edited in May 2026; it states explicitly 以下は2026年5月撮影。税抜きで記載しています — photographed May 2026, listed WITHOUT tax. So these are recent figures, but add 10% at the till. Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ HOW THIS SHOP WORKS, WHICH DETERMINES WHAT YOU CAN ACTUALLY ORDER: it is a 立ち飲み — you stand. Ordering is 口頭注文・伝票式の後払い, spoken to the staff, tallied on a slip, paid at the end. Cash only, no cover charge, non-smoking, one unisex toilet. And most of the food is not on any fixed menu at all: the article reports the owner, Inoue-san, visits seven or eight suppliers every morning and prices that day’s catch that day, so 黒板には、お刺身をはじめ約40種類が50円〜600円台 — roughly forty blackboard items between 50 yen and the 600s, different every day. The blackboard items below are examples the writer photographed over several visits, marked ※日替り, not a standing list. ⚠ THE DIETARY SHAPE: a Japanese standing bar of this type is raw fish plus deep-fried things, and both halves are a problem. The fried side — ハムカツ, the 串揚げ set — is panko and batter, i.e. wheat, in shared oil. The raw side is fish. There is no vegetable dish on any published list except a tuna salad, which is tuna. ⚠ AND ONE DRINK TRAP WORTH THE WHOLE ENTRY: ホッピー is not a soft drink and not a mixer in the harmless sense — it is a near-beer brewed from BARLEY MALT, sold as a set with a glass of shochu to mix into. Foreigners order it constantly believing it is the low-alcohol safe option. It is barley. The 黒糖焼酎 on the same list, distilled from sugarcane muscovado, is the opposite: no grain at all.

items.en: Ham cutlet — a slab of ham crumbed and deep-fried. The house speciality, and the thing the article names when it says order something substantial
items.note: カツ＝小麦粉＋卵＋パン粉の衣、共用油。Flour, egg and panko breadcrumbs, fried in oil shared with everything else fried here. Pork. Nothing about this is negotiable.

items.ja: 串揚げほろ酔いセット
items.en: The tipsy set — one drink plus six kushiage skewers chosen by the kitchen
items.note: 串揚げは全て小麦粉・パン粉の衣、油も共用。おまかせ＝中身は選べない。Every skewer is battered and crumbed in wheat and fried in one shared oil, and the six are the kitchen’s choice, so you cannot even steer it towards vegetables. The included drink is unspecified.

items.en: Tuna salad — the standing bar’s vegetable dish: sliced onion under a heap of tuna, in a sweet-sharp dressing, with mayonnaise on the side. Marked ※日替り
items.note: THE ONLY SALAD ON THE LIST AND IT IS A FISH DISH. ツナ＝魚、マヨ付き＝卵。The article describes the dressing as 甘辛くさっぱり, sweet-and-sharp — at a Japanese izakaya that combination is normally soy-based, which would make it wheat as well. Ask.

items.en: A small set of hand-formed sushi, when it appears. Marked ※日替り
items.note: Fish on vinegared rice — no wheat in the components themselves; the soy sauce you dip it in is the wheat. Some nigiri arrive pre-brushed with ニキリ (a reduced soy glaze), which puts it inside the dish. Ask which. Fish.

items.en: Bluefin tuna belly, cut thick — the article calls it the one blackboard item not to miss
items.note: Raw fish; the wheat is in the dipping soy, which is poured by you.

items.en: Live whelk — sea snail, sliced and served raw
items.note: 巻貝＝軟体動物。A mollusc, which matters for a shellfish allergy in a way “fish” does not. Raw and unseasoned; the soy is on the side.
Which three is decided by that morning’s buying. Fish; soy on the side.

items.en: Ara-jiru — soup made from the bones, head and collar left after the fish is filleted. Fifty yen, which is the article’s headline astonishment
items.note: あら＝魚のアラ、味噌または醤油仕立て。Fish bones are the entire dish, so this is as far from vegetarian as a soup gets. Seasoned with miso or soy; the miso may be barley, which Japanese labelling law does not require anyone to declare. Ask which.

items.ja: ミニ本まぐろ中落ち丼
items.en: Small bowl of bluefin scraped from the bone over rice — made in tiny numbers, gone early
items.price: 650円（税抜、2026年5月・日替り、数量限定）
items.note: 中落ち＝中骨に残った身。Tuna scraped off the backbone, over rice. Wheat only via the soy, unless the bowl arrives pre-sauced — ask.

items.en: Hoppy set — a bottle of Hoppy with a jug of shochu to mix, poured strong here: the article reckons the shochu measure takes three refills of Hoppy
items.note: ⚠ ホッピーは大麦麦芽で造るビールテイスト飲料。THE TRAP DRINK. Hoppy looks and is sold like a mixer, and travellers order it as the light option — it is a beer-taste beverage brewed from BARLEY MALT, so it is exactly as much of a gluten problem as beer. The shochu it is mixed with may or may not be barley too; that is not published. Plant-based, but not gluten-free.

items.en: Draught beer — Premium Malt’s, per the article’s list of what is on
items.note: ビール＝大麦麦芽。Barley malt.

items.en: Chuhai — shochu with soda, the cheapest drink in the house and where the price list starts
items.note: 焼酎の原料（芋・麦・米）は未掲載。Shochu and soda. Whether the shochu base is sweet potato, barley or rice is not published, and barley shochu is common — distillation removes gluten protein in practice, but if you avoid barley outright, ask which bottle. Plant-based.

items.en: Asahi kokuto shochu, from Asahi Shuzo on Kikaijima — the article’s writer takes it with soda
items.note: 黒糖焼酎＝サトウキビの黒糖が原料、穀物不使用。Kokuto shochu is distilled from sugarcane muscovado, not grain at all — the one spirit on this list with no barley, wheat or rice in it even before distillation. Legally it may only be made on the Amami islands. Plant-based.

items.en: Ginban sake, one gō (180ml) — the Toyama brewery, poured here as the thing to drink with the tuna
items.note: 日本酒は米・米麹・水が基本。ただし本醸造は醸造アルコール添加、grade未掲載。Sake is rice, rice koji and water — no barley, no wheat. The one caveat is grade: a 本醸造 has distilled brewer’s alcohol added, and its base is not declared on a standing-bar blackboard. If the bottle says 純米 it is rice only. Ask, or ask for junmai.

tokyo_asanoya.price_note: ⚠ START WITH THE SOBA WARNING, BECAUSE IT APPLIES TO FOUR OF THE SIX ITEMS: Japanese soba is conventionally 二八, eight parts buckwheat to TWO PARTS WHEAT, and only noodles explicitly sold as 十割 are pure buckwheat. 淺野屋 declares no ratio. Buckwheat being naturally gluten-free is the most dangerous half-truth in Japanese dining, and a soba counter is not a safe room for a coeliac unless it says 十割 on the wall. The つゆ compounds it: dashi, soy and mirin means bonito (FISH) and wheat. ⭐ THE MOST QUOTABLE FACT ON THE MENU IS THE 150円 GAP BETWEEN もり AND ざる. They are the same noodles and the same broth. ざる costs 650円 and もり costs 500円, and the entire difference is a pinch of shredded nori on top — the distinction is a survival from Edo-period soba stalls, where ざる was served on a bamboo screen with a better-grade tsuyu, and what remains of it today is the seaweed. Knowing that is worth 150円 every time. ⚠ AND THE ITEM THAT LOOKS SAFEST IS MADE ENTIRELY OF WHEAT: 冷したぬき. たぬき — "raccoon dog" — is not an animal and not a vegetable; it is 天かす, the loose scraps of TEMPURA BATTER skimmed off the fryer, scattered over the noodles. The English "Cold Tanuki Set" conveys none of that, and a reader avoiding gluten has no way to guess that the topping is pure fried wheat flour. It is, however, one of the few Japanese noodle toppings with no animal in it, which is exactly the wrong kind of reassurance. ON THE LISTING: six items, no 更新日, undated. Recorded average spend 1,000–1,999円. Open 11:00–15:00 MONDAY TO FRIDAY ONLY, closed Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays — a Kanda office-district lunch counter, so it does not exist for a weekend visitor. 31 seats, 神田猿楽町2-7-6.

items.en: Mori soba — cold soba with dipping broth, no seaweed. The cheapest thing in the shop
items.note: ⚠ 二八そばの可能性が高い（十割の表示なし）。つゆは出汁・醤油＝魚・小麦。The noodle is ask because the wheat ratio is undeclared — assume 20% wheat. The dip is bonito dashi and soy, so it is fish and wheat regardless of what the noodle turns out to be. Ask about both separately.

items.en: Zaru soba — the identical bowl with shredded nori over it, 150円 more
items.note: ⭐ THE ONLY DIFFERENCE FROM もり IS THE NORI. Same noodles, same tsuyu, same caveats — 150円 buys you a sprinkle of seaweed and the ghost of an Edo-period grading that no longer exists. Nori itself is plant and gluten-free, so it changes nothing dietary.

items.en: Tororo soba — soba with grated mountain yam
items.note: Grated yam adds nothing animal, so this stays at the same ask/ask as the plain bowls: it turns on the flour ratio and the tsuyu, not the topping. ⚠ Raw grated yam causes mouth and skin irritation in a substantial minority of people — a known nuisance, not an allergy, but worth expecting.

items.en: Soba served in small divided portions — the name suggests the Izumo 割子 style of stacked lacquer bowls, but the shop does not describe it
items.note: ⚠ THE ONE ITEM ON THIS MENU I CANNOT PIN DOWN AND AM NOT GOING TO GUESS AT. The Chinese listing preserves the kanji 小割蕎麥 and the Korean transliterates it rather than translating, which together confirm the written form 小割 but not the reading or the format. 割子そば is an Izumo speciality of stacked small bowls eaten in sequence, and 小割 plausibly refers to that — but this is a Kanda shop, not a Shimane one, and no source here says so. Recorded as UNVERIFIED in form; the dietary caveats are the same soba ones regardless.

items.en: Mini pork-cutlet rice bowl with soba — the standard Japanese noodle-shop set
items.note: ⚠ 三重の小麦：そば（二八）・パン粉・つゆ。THREE separate wheat sources in one tray: the soba binder, the PANKO on the cutlet, and the soy in both the katsudon sauce and the noodle broth. PORK and EGG (katsudon is finished with beaten egg). The most expensive item on the menu and the least available to anyone with a restriction.

items.en: Cold tanuki soba set — chilled noodles scattered with crisp tempura-batter scraps
items.note: ⚠ たぬき＝天かす＝揚げた小麦の衣。NOT AN ANIMAL. "Tanuki" here means TENKASU — the loose scraps of tempura batter skimmed off the fryer — so the topping is pure fried wheat flour and this is the clearest "no" on the menu for a coeliac, despite sounding like the innocuous option. Marked ask rather than no on vegan because tenkasu itself is flour, water and oil with no animal, but the batter frequently contains EGG and the fryer is shared with prawn.
